This document runs the ODE parameter fitting for the article: Anthony W. Waddle et al., 'Heated homes for hoppers: Hotspot shelters enable frogs to survive chytridiomycosis and stimulate resistance'.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = F, warning = F)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(minpack.lm) # For the fitting
library(deSolve)
library(tibble)

# Data and model filepaths
compartmental_filename <- "data/expdata_compartments.csv"
perfrog_filename <- "data/expdata_perfrog.csv"
source("chytrid_model.R")

# Set the ggplot theme
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 12))
options(ggplot2.discrete.colour = brewer.pal(7, "Dark2"), ggplot2.discrete.fill = brewer.pal(7, "Dark2"))
```

## Experimental data

The data is from from `r compartmental_filename` and `r perfrog_filename`, which 
are generated using the `process_frog_compartments.R` script.
There are 8 Mesocosms, 4 shaded and 4 unshaded.
We assume at T=0 there were 5 frogs in each of the following categories:

- infect.+vacc. (IV1)
- susc.+vacc. (SV)
- infect. (I1)
- susc. (S)

and all other compartments had 0 frogs.

```{r read-data, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3}
# Read in the two experimental datasets
# per-compartment timeseries, and per-frog data
# We expect the per-compartment data to have the following columns:
#   - Mesocosm: the mesocosm ID
#   - shaded: true/false whether the mesocosm was shaded or unshaded
#   - week: the observation week
#   - compartment: the compartment label
#   - N: the number of frogs
percompartment <- read.csv(compartmental_filename,check.names=F) %>%
  mutate(Mesocosm=as.factor(Mesocosm)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from=compartment,values_from=N) %>%
  mutate(across(-c(Mesocosm,shaded,week),~ifelse(is.na(.x),0,.x))) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(N = sum(c_across(-c(Mesocosm,shaded,week)))) %>%
  ungroup()
# We expect the per-frog data to have the following columns:
#   - Mesocosm: the mesocosm ID
#   - shaded: true/false whether the mesocosm was shaded or unshaded
#   - frog_id: the unique ID of the frog
#   - week: the observation week
#   - vaccinated: true/false whether the frog was vaccinated at week 0
#   - inf_level: the recorded infection level at this observation
#   - compartment_i: numeric of compartment (0-S/SV, 1-I1/IV1, 2-I2/IV2, 3-I3/IV3)
#   - prev_infection: if the frog has been infected since week 0
#   - compartment: current compartment label for the frog
perfrog <- read.csv(perfrog_filename,check.names = F) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(inf_level))
# Vector of observation weeks
weeks = sort(unique(perfrog$week))

# Plot the number of frogs observed over time
group_by(perfrog,Mesocosm,shaded,week) %>%
  summarise(N=n(),.groups="drop") %>%
ggplot(aes(x=week,y=N,colour=shaded,group=Mesocosm)) + 
  geom_point() + geom_line() +
  labs(y="No. frogs found") + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,20)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,15),breaks = weeks, minor_breaks = NULL)
```

## Model

We use the following model (Fig. S5, mortality not shown in diagram):

```{r model-diagram, out.width = "400px"}
knitr::include_graphics("model_diagram_20230925.png")
```

We make the following assumptions on the parameters we are fitting in the model:

1.  Frogs die from any compartment at a mortality rate $\mu$, which is invariant to compartment, vaccination, and environment
2.  The effect of vaccination ($\alpha$) is invariant to environment 
3. The recovery rate ($\omega$) is invariant to vaccination and environment
3. The transmission rate ($\beta$) varies between environments.


The model equations are: $$\begin{aligned}
  \frac{dS}{dt}   &= -\beta S \frac{I}{(N-1)} - \mu S \\
  \frac{dI_1}{dt}  &= \beta S \frac{I}{(N-1)} - (\gamma_1+\mu) I_1 \\
  \frac{dI_2}{dt}  &= \gamma_1 I_1 - (\gamma_2+\mu) I_2 \\
  \frac{dI_3}{dt}  &= \gamma_2 I_2 - (\omega+\mu) I_3 \\
  \frac{dS_V}{dt}  &= -\alpha \beta S_V \frac{I}{(N-1)} + \omega I_{V3} + \omega I_3 - \mu S_V \\
  \frac{dI_{V1}}{dt} &= \alpha \beta S_V \frac{I}{(N-1)} - (\gamma_1+\mu) I_{V1} \\
  \frac{dI_{V2}}{dt} &= \gamma_1 I_{V1} - (\gamma_2+\mu) I_{V2} \\
  \frac{dI_{V3}}{dt} &= \gamma_2 I_{V2} - (\omega+\mu) I_{V3} \\
  \frac{dN}{dt} &= -\mu (S+I_1+I_2+I_3+S_V+I_{V1}+I_{V2}+I_{V3})
\end{aligned}$$

## Parameter fitting

```{r fit-params}
# Original guesses
unknown_params = list(
  beta_shaded = parameters[["beta"]],
  beta_greenhouse = parameters[["beta"]],
  alpha=parameters[["alpha"]], 
  omega = parameters[["omega"]],
  mu = parameters[["mu"]]
)

# Fit model
fit=nls.lm(par=unknown_params,lower=c(0,0,0,0,0),fn=calc_residuals,expdata=percompartment)
summfit <- summary(fit)
fit_coefficients <- summfit$coefficients

# Print full details of coefficient fits
kable(fit_coefficients,caption="Estimated parameters",digits=3)
```

Estimate and 95% CI (Table 1 in the article):

```{r table-fits-CI}
full_join(
  rownames_to_column(data.frame(fit_coefficients), var="Parameter"),
  rownames_to_column(data.frame(confint(fit),check.names=F), var="Parameter"),
  by="Parameter"
) %>%
  mutate(`95% CI` = paste0("(",round(`2.5 %`,digits=3),", ",
                           round(`97.5 %`,digits=3),")")) %>%
  select(Parameter,Estimate,`95% CI`) %>%
  kable(digits=3)
```

Plots comparing the fits to the experimental data (Fig. S6 in article):

```{r plot-fits}
# Get the parameters from the fit for plotting
fit_params = summfit$coefficients[,"Estimate"]
parameters["alpha"] = fit_params[["alpha"]]
parameters["omega"] = fit_params[["omega"]]
parameters["mu"] = fit_params["mu"]

# Function to plot the compartments against the solution
lab_fn <- function(labels) {
  gsub("(\\a)|(V*\\d)|(V)","\\1[\\2\\3]",labels)
}
plot_compartments <- function(parameters, env_shaded) {
  prediction <- ode(
        func=chytrid.ode.model,
        y=x0,
        times=seq(0,max(percompartment$week),length.out=100),
        parms=parameters
      ) %>% as_tibble() %>%
        mutate(across(everything(),as.numeric)) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols=-time) %>%
    mutate(name=lab_fn(name)) %>%
    filter(name != "N")
  plot_title = ifelse(env_shaded,"Shaded","Unshaded")
  plot_data <- percompartment %>% 
    pivot_longer(cols=!c(Mesocosm,shaded,week)) %>%
    filter(shaded == env_shaded) %>%
    filter(name != "N") %>%
    rename(time="week") %>%
    mutate(name = lab_fn(name))
  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x=time,y=value)) + 
      geom_line(aes(group=Mesocosm),alpha=0.5) + 
      geom_point(aes(group=Mesocosm,colour="Data"),alpha=0.7) +
      geom_line(aes(colour="Prediction"),size=1,data=prediction) +
      facet_wrap(~name, labeller="label_parsed") +
      scale_colour_manual(values=c("black","#1B9E77")) +
      labs(title=plot_title,x="Time (weeks)",y="Number of frogs",colour=NULL)+
      theme(legend.position=c(0.85,0.15))
}

# Unshaded/Greenhouse
parameters["beta"] = fit_params[["beta_greenhouse"]]
plot_compartments(parameters,env_shaded=FALSE)
# Shaded
parameters["beta"] = fit_params[["beta_shaded"]]
plot_compartments(parameters,env_shaded=TRUE)
```

The two further values given in the article text:

-   the ratio of beta shaded:unshaded (greenhouse), $\frac{\beta_{SH}}{\beta_{UN}}$, which is: `r round(fit_coefficients["beta_shaded","Estimate"]/fit_coefficients["beta_greenhouse","Estimate"],digits=1)`.

-   The inverse of $\alpha$, which is: `r round(1/fit_coefficients["alpha","Estimate"],digits=4)`
